messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: support of categorical distribution
parts:
In Bugs example vol1/inhalers, the response is modeled as
categorical distribution, i.e.,
y ~ categorical(p).

Currently if p is of length N, the support for y is {0, 1, ..., N-1}.
In Bugs/JAGS, it is {1, 2, ..., N}.
Should we follow Bugs/JAGS convention?

Now using the exact data from Bugs example, I am using
y - 1 ~ categorical(p)

--
JIqiang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] support of categorical distribution
parts:
On 2/20/12 2:54 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> In Bugs example vol1/inhalers, the response is modeled as
> categorical distribution, i.e.,
> y ~ categorical(p).
>
> Currently if p is of length N, the support for y is {0, 1, ..., N-1}.
> In Bugs/JAGS, it is {1, 2, ..., N}.
> Should we follow Bugs/JAGS convention?

We followed the conventions in BDA (which match
the Wikipedia in this case).

It seems to make more sense to use 1...N
rather than 0...(N-1) because we index from 1
and then the categorical will match the multinomial.

But then the Bernoulli uses 0 and 1. Can't tell
what BDA would do for that because it only has
the binomial.

What does everyone else think?

If we follow BDA, we need to doc this in a section
BUGS/JAGS vs. Stan conventions.

> Now using the exact data from Bugs example, I am using
> y - 1 ~ categorical(p)

That should work for now (and in the future if we stick
with the BDA convention).

- Bob

On Feb 20, 4:47 pm, Bob Carpenter <c...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> It seems to make more sense to use 1...N
> rather than 0...(N-1) because we index from 1
> and then the categorical will match the multinomial.
>
> But then the Bernoulli uses 0 and 1.  Can't tell
> what BDA would do for that because it only has
> the binomial.
>
> What does everyone else think?

Put me down for using zero iff the outcome variable can be analyzed as
ratio-scale. Sometimes ratio-scale kind of makes sense for binary
variables, but it's hard to come up with an example where it makes
sense with more than two categories.
